asil_justification.dependency_note: The integrity of this interface is bounded by FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004, which are themselves recorded as not_applicable for the reason that they are security requirements. This requirement therefore rests, for its integrity, on two requirements that carry no ASIL of their own. That dependency is recorded here so that it is visible; it is not itself a justification of the marking being correct, and this field does not assert that the dependency has been discharged.
asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'interface'. It specifies what the item publishes and when it refuses a state request; the refusal path is specified, but the requirement is not itself the specification of a reaction to a hazardous event, and no safety goal in this corpus allocates this interface to one. ISO 26262 allocates an ASIL to a requirement derived from a hazardous event, so not_applicable is the schema's own enumerated value for that case.
asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product and not a claim that the interface's integrity has been demonstrated.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.

record_verbatim.rationale: The system-level statement of the integration contract with the vehicle manufacturer. It resolves the tension named in the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000004 in one direction and states the direction explicitly, because a requirement that said only 'the item honours state requests' would leave the safety case resting on the item being overridden cleanly, and 'cleanly' is not a property any record here establishes. The publication half is separated from the refusal half deliberately: publication is a capability the vehicle manufacturer needs in every mode, and refusal is a safety behaviour that only exists when the item has already judged something unsafe.

revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
